title: Cohomological Brown representability on the adic localizing hull
statement:
Fix a universe u, a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ in universe u of positive
characteristic different from $\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme X, and a
commutative condensed coefficient ring $\Lambda$ with the certificate of one of the
three adic families [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting; def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate].
Let $\mathcal L_X$ be the full localizing hull of the bounded constructible objects
inside the ordinary unbounded category $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{p_X^*\Lambda})$,
with ambient coproducts indexed in universe u+1
[def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure]. For every additive-group-valued
cohomological functor $H:\mathcal L_X^{op}\to\mathrm{Ab}_{u+1}$ which sends
all these coproducts to products, the underlying set-valued functor of H is
representable by an object of $\mathcal L_X$.

proof.text: The module-object category is Grothendieck abelian, using the sectionwise module-sheaf equivalence if needed. Its derived category is well generated by Neeman, On the derived category of sheaves on a manifold, Theorem 0.2. This theorem concerns arbitrary Grothendieck abelian categories and requires no finite cohomological-dimension hypothesis on k.

The admissible constructible hearts have a small set of models. Fix a small site. Covers and finite presentation matrices give small data; descent isomorphisms on pairwise overlaps and their triple-overlap cocycle equalities are choices in Hom sets. Finite stratifications contribute small data as well. Glue the open-stratum and closed-complement sheaves by the localization exact sequence; the extension classes of two fixed sheaves lie in a degree-one derived Hom set. Induct on the number of strata. A bounded constructible complex is assembled from its finitely many cohomology sheaves by truncation triangles. At each step choices are classified by a Hom set. Induction on the cohomological interval and union over its integer endpoints give an essentially small Dbc. This is the finite-presentation argument of det-brown-hypotheses-small, applied directly to the constructibility predicate in Lean. Choose a small skeleton S.

The intersection defining the displayed hull is precisely the localizing subcategory generated by S. It is well generated by Krause, Localization theory for triangulated categories, Theorem 7.2.1: choose a common uncountable regular cardinal making the ambient category well generated and the set S alpha-compact. Its alpha-localizing closure provides alpha-small perfect generators. Theorem 5.1.1 then represents H. The skeleton, Hom sets and values of H use the same universe u+1. No compact-generation claim about Dbc over a general k is used.
